text:
lee: hey team, first-week quick Q i made a short 'first week cheatsheet' while pairing with my manager. where should it live so others can use it? My Pages? Team Docs? Templates?

devex-liaison: welcome Lee! good question. short answer: start in My Pages, then request publication. long answer: if it's a one-off personal guide put it in My Pages and favorite it. if it's reusable across hires, ask docs maintainers to publish it as a Template in /Templates/engineering or as an onboarding supplement under /Company Templates/Onboarding.

lee: what does publication involve? i don't want to break links or lose comments when it moves.

devex-liaison: publication is a manual step by the docs team. workflow we use: 1) Draft in My Pages and add required properties: Owner, Status: Proposal, Tags (multi-select), Slug. 2) Run `@doc-bot review-template <notion-link> short-summary` in this channel. 3) Docs maintainers will lint the page (links, image hosts, properties) and then publish a Template or copy into /Company Templates. Move preserves comments/backlinks, but maintainers handle the Template button wiring.

lee: got it. i actually tried duplicating a page and dropping it into /Templates/engineering but the template button didn't appear for others.

olivia: duplicating usually doesn't keep the Template metadata. The Template button is a special Notion configuration pointing to a Template page in the Templates space. Maintainers create the canonical Template so the button works for everyone. Copying into /Templates by hand can leave stale properties.

lee: are there naming rules? searchability is my main concern.

devex-liaison: yes we prefer human readable titles prefixed by team: `eng-infra - First week cheatsheet - 2026`. Also add a slug property like `eng-infra/first-week-cheatsheet`. For templates add Tags: onboarding, first-week, quickstart. That helps our docs indexer.

lee: i might need edit access to iterate with reviewers for a few days. do we grant temporary edit rights?

doc-bot: To request edit access run: `@doc-bot request-access <notion-link> reason:"template iteration" duration:7d`. Typical workflow: Editor rights for 7 days, then reverted to Viewer. Include the reviewers you'll work with.

lee: perfect. quick question about content style: do we prefer short checklist or mini-runbook?

devex-liaison: checklist is fine for a cheatsheet. If it grows beyond ~500 words or includes step-by-step commands consider turning it into a runbook with sections (Overview, Steps, Rollback, Contacts). Add a short "When to use this" blurb at top so maintainers can categorize it.

lee: any gotchas I should watch for (images, external links)?

doc-librarian: avoid embedding internal VM credentials/screenshots with secrets. Use secure links (redwood.internal links) for internal tools. Prefer screenshots hosted in the docs assets bucket (our docs-librarian will mirror images). Large attachments can slow publish; we prefer short screenshots + links. Also run `@doc-bot link-check <page-link>` before review to catch broken refs.

lee: thanks. i'll draft in My Pages with the properties and then `@doc-bot review-template` here.

doc-bot: Action created: review-template request by lee for https://redwood.notion.so/lee/first-week-cheatsheet. Ticket DOCS-777 assigned to docs-maintainers. Lint: pending.

olivia: tiny tip add a short "Who to ping" section with names/teams (e.g., @devex-liaison, infra-oncall) so new hires know who to DM. makes life easier for the reviewers too.

lee: will do, thanks all! :wave:
